performed_via_github_app.description:
# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

🤖 **Salvage note — duplicate-pair disposition (protocol §8)** · task 13060, lane code-d

Canonical PR: **PR #7734** (`richTerminalBytesForKey`, branch `queue/13060-787-kitty-encoder`, head e10e3a2f2e) — bound to live task 13060.
Sibling/duplicate: **PR #7348** (`kittyBytesForKey`, branch `queue/12634-787-slice-c`, head d7dc062cd9) — same Slice C of issue #787, same two files (`pkgs/id/web/src/world-keyboard.ts`, `world-keyboard.test.ts`).

I diffed both PRs in full this shift (not a file-list comparison). Findings:

- **Nothing unique in PR #7348 needs lifting into PR #7734.** PR #7734 is the more complete implementation: it adds F1–F12 tilde forms (PR #7348 returns null for F5), Insert, and a larger fixture-mirrored test suite (world-keyboard 22/22; full web suite 669 passed / 9 skipped; tsc clean — recorded by the previous holder and re-verified as the PR head this shift).
- Caps-Lock case preservation, which PR #7348 calls out explicitly, is already the canonical behaviour: with Shift not held, PR #7734 does not unshift, so Ctrl+`A` (Caps Lock) encodes as `CSI 65 ; 5 u`, matching PR #7348.
- PR #7348 sends Alt+multi-scalar input (e.g. Alt+😀) as a single CSI-u codepoint; PR #7734 intentionally keeps multi-scalar input on the text path per design §4.4 (Codex-dispositioned on this PR). Declined — deliberate divergence, not a gap.
- One flagged divergence, explicitly declined: for shifted scalars on non-US layouts (e.g. AZERTY Shift+`1`), PR #7348 drops Shift from the modifier parameter to avoid the decoder's US-table remap. PR #7734 instead unshifts only when Shift produced the scalar and keeps the full modifier parameter, following the kitty-disambiguate-v1 fixture expectations (Slice D's parity oracle is the place to settle any residual decoder mismatch). Not lifted.

Disposition: PR #7348 stays open for now only because neither PR may merge/close until CI completes (both PRs' checks have been QUEUED since 2026-11-08T14:48–15:16Z in the systemic runner backlog). Once CI is green on PR #7734 and it merges, PR #7348 should be closed as the duplicate with a link to this note; its branch is the salvage source until then — do not delete it by hand.
